item.title: [AMZN Neutral (-0.14)] Watch how an Amazon drone delivery in Texas ended up in a pool

item.title: [NVDA Neutral (+0.11)] Which Streaming Stock Would Hold Up Better in a Recession: Netflix or Walt Disney?
item.description:
Sentiment: NVDA Neutral (+0.11)
In a potential recession, streaming services are expected to be resilient as low-cost entertainment. Between Netflix and Walt Disney, Netflix is positioned to hold up better due to its pure-play streaming model. Disney's lucrative experiences segment, which accounts for a significant portion of its operating income, makes it more vulnerable to economic downturns as consumers cut back on expensive travel and theme park visits.

item.title: [NVDA Bullish (+0.43)] Hut 8 Stock Draws Bullish Wall Street Targets On Nvidia AI Deal

item.title: [AAPL Neutral (+0.13), MSFT Neutral (+0.12), NVDA Bullish (+0.25)] Alphabet and Nvidia Own More SpaceX Than BlackRock and Vanguard Combined. Here's Why That's About to Change.
item.category: AAPL Neutral (+0.13), MSFT Neutral (+0.12), NVDA Bullish (+0.25)
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Neutral (+0.13), MSFT Neutral (+0.12), NVDA Bullish (+0.25)
Alphabet and Nvidia currently hold more shares in SpaceX than BlackRock and Vanguard combined, largely due to early investments and conversions from other ventures like xAI. However, this ownership landscape is set to shift significantly as more SpaceX shares are unlocked and made available to the public, leading major investment firms to increase their stakes. While early investors may not immediately offload their shares, the increased float will gradually allow large asset managers like BlackRock and Vanguard to become dominant shareholders, especially once SpaceX is potentially added to the S&P 500.

item.title: [AMZN Neutral (+0.11)] Walmart stock drops 9% as sales growth slows, customers make 'trade-offs' amid high fuel costs
item.description:

The company attributed this deceleration partly to high fuel costs prompting consumers to make "trade-offs" and lower drug prices affecting health and wellness sales. Walmart is focusing on price cuts and benefiting from tariff refunds to attract cost-conscious shoppers, with its e-commerce sales showing strong growth.

item.title: [AMZN Bearish (-0.25)] CareCloud Breach Expands From Eight-Hour Incident to 3.7 Million Patients
item.description:
Sentiment: AMZN Bearish (-0.25)
Five months after a security incident, CareCloud has confirmed that a data breach affecting 3.7 million patients occurred between March 10 and March 16, 2026. Initially believed to be an eight-hour disruption, the incident involved attackers exfiltrating sensitive medical and financial data from CareCloud's Amazon Web Services environment. The stolen information includes Social Security numbers, health insurance details, and payment card information, posing significant long-term risks to affected individuals.

item.title: [MSFT Neutral (+0.10), AMZN Neutral (+0.13)] A look at HTTP's new QUERY method
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Neutral (+0.10), AMZN Neutral (+0.13)
In June 2026, HTTP introduced the new QUERY method, a general-purpose standard defined in RFC 10008, designed to handle large or complex read operations. This method provides a safe and idempotent alternative to GET and POST for queries, carrying content in the request body without altering server state. It offers greater reliability, observability, and compliance for repeatable queries, addressing limitations of traditional methods like URL size constraints and operational ambiguity.

item.title: [NVDA Bullish (+0.32)] Paul Tudor Jones Just Liquidated His Entire Stake in Applied Materials Stock. I Don’t Think He’s 100% Bearish on AI Though… Yet
item.description:

However, the author argues that Jones is not entirely bearish on AI, as he significantly increased his positions in Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM) and Nvidia (NVDA) during the same period. This suggests a rotation of gains into other AI companies offering potentially higher growth at a lower cost, rather than a broad bearish bet against AI.

item.title: [AAPL Neutral (-0.13)] Zuckerberg's manifesto: Do Meta's promises and actions align?
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Neutral (-0.13)
Mark Zuckerberg's "AI manifesto," "The Future is for Everyone," outlines a vision of democratized AI and personal superintelligence agents. However, the article questions whether Meta's past actions and current capabilities align with this ambitious vision, particularly concerning its commitment to open-source principles and its standing in the competitive AI landscape. It suggests that Meta's public stance might be more of a PR move to position itself amidst stronger AI contenders.

item.title: [NVDA Neutral (+0.12)] IBIT's 0.25% Fee Sells Off Bitcoin Daily, and the Prospectus Calls Every Sale a Taxable Event
item.description:
Sentiment: NVDA Neutral (+0.12)
The iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT) charges a 0.25% sponsor fee by selling a portion of its Bitcoin holdings daily, which its prospectus explicitly states is a taxable event for shareholders. This mechanism means investors could incur tax liabilities even without selling their IBIT shares, due to the trust realizing tiny gains or losses on their behalf. While IBIT offers higher liquidity, cheaper alternatives like Franklin's EZBC and Bitwise's BITB exist, though they operate with the same daily-sale tax mechanic.

item.title: [MSFT Bullish (+0.29)] Storage modernization: Supermicro and partners on AI
item.description:

The companies are working to modernize storage environments by focusing on performance, flexibility, and efficiency, rather than just capacity. This involves providing software layers for data orchestration, developing high-capacity and efficient QLC SSDs, and adopting industry standards like NVMe over Fabrics to ensure seamless data movement and optimize GPU utilization for AI workloads.

item.description:

item.description:

Qualcomm (QCOM) reported mixed fiscal third-quarter 2026 results, with revenues exceeding expectations but earnings falling short, primarily due to strong automotive growth contrasting with weakness in its handset business. The company saw record automotive revenues, surging 61% year-over-year, while handset revenues declined by 20% due to inventory adjustments and memory constraints. Qualcomm is also increasing its investment in data center solutions, though near-term profitability remains pressured by input costs and mobile demand.

item.title: [AAPL Bearish (-0.24)] Is QCOM Stock a Buy as Auto and AI Growth Offset Handset Weakness?
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Bearish (-0.24)
Qualcomm (QCOM) is diversifying its business by expanding into automotive, IoT, and data center computing to counteract weakening handset sales, particularly from Apple. While non-handset revenues are growing significantly and are expected to represent over half of Qualcomm CDMA Technologies revenues by fiscal 2027, this shift comes with increased product costs and lower margins in the short term. Despite trading at a discount compared to its historical valuation, the stock's overall appeal remains balanced due to ongoing handset pressures and margin dilution, warranting a "Hold" rating from Zacks.

item.title: [MSFT Bullish (+0.33), AMZN Bullish (+0.32)] Meta Falls Far Behind Amazon, Alphabet, and Microsoft In AI
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Bullish (+0.33), AMZN Bullish (+0.32)
Meta's market capitalization of $1.39 trillion significantly lags behind Amazon ($2.87 trillion), Microsoft ($3.60 trillion), and Alphabet ($4.19 trillion) in the AI race, despite CEO Mark Zuckerberg's 14-page AI manifesto. Even private AI rival Anthropic is nearing or surpassing Meta's valuation, highlighting investors' diminished view of Meta's social media business and AI strategy compared to its tech giant peers. The article emphasizes market cap as a crucial indicator of investor confidence in the AI supremacy battle, noting that legacy businesses are becoming less relevant as AI's importance grows.

item.title: [AMZN Bullish (+0.80)] If You Invested $1000 In Amazon.com Stock 15 Years Ago, You Would Have This Much Today
item.description:
Sentiment: AMZN Bullish (+0.80)
This article highlights the significant returns an investment in Amazon.com stock would have yielded over 15 years. An initial investment of $1,000 in AMZN 15 years ago would now be worth over $27,000, demonstrating the power of compounded returns. Amazon.com has outperformed the market with an average annual return of 24.36% over this period.

item.title: [AMZN Neutral (+0.14)] Delta chose Amazon over Starlink, Musk responds
item.description:
Sentiment: AMZN Neutral (+0.14)
Delta Air Lines chose Amazon's satellite WiFi over Starlink for its inflight connectivity, a decision Elon Musk claims will lead to passenger losses. Delta's CEO defends the choice, citing brand integration, while Musk points to passengers switching airlines. Other airlines, however, are adopting Starlink, raising concerns about Delta's competitive position if it doesn't offer comparable WiFi.

item.title: [MSFT Bullish (+0.27)] Microsoft’s Original Xbox Is Back As A Massive Mattel Brick Set
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Bullish (+0.27)
Microsoft is celebrating the Xbox's 25th anniversary by partnering with Mattel to release a massive brick set that recreates the original Xbox console and its iconic "The Duke" controller. The set, priced at $329.99, includes 3,509 pieces and modules celebrating games like Halo: Combat Evolved, Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind, and Psychonauts, with interactive lighting effects tied to soundtracks. This release complements a limited edition Xbox Series X25 featuring the classic translucent green colorway.

item.title: [MSFT Neutral (+0.10)] IT vs. OT: Key differences explained
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Neutral (+0.10)
This article explains the key differences between Information Technology (IT) and Operational Technology (OT), highlighting that IT focuses on data while OT manages physical industrial operations. It discusses the growing convergence of IT and OT, driven by IoT and AI, which offers benefits like cost reduction and enhanced security, despite challenges such as device inventory, legacy systems, and data integration. The piece elaborates on the examples and use cases for both IT and OT, emphasizing how their convergence can lead to greater efficiencies and better decision-making processes.

item.title: [AMZN Neutral (+0.15)] Walmart beats Street on Q2 EPS, revenues; misses on U.S. comp sales
item.description:
Sentiment: AMZN Neutral (+0.15)
Walmart reported strong Q2 fiscal 2027 results, exceeding analyst expectations for total revenues of $187.9 billion and adjusted EPS of $0.81. However, the company missed U.S. comparative sales forecasts, with a rise of only 2.6% against predictions of 3.7-3.8%. E-commerce sales and the advertising business were highlights, showing significant growth.

item.title: [AAPL Bearish (-0.24)] QCOM Falls 30.6% in 3 Months as Handset Risks Challenge Auto Growth
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Bearish (-0.24)
Qualcomm (QCOM) shares have dropped 30.6% in the last three months due to weakening handset demand and near-term margin pressures. While the company is experiencing significant growth in its automotive and data center segments, with automotive revenues up 61% and plans for $15 billion in data center revenues by fiscal 2029, concerns remain about whether this diversification can offset the ongoing mobile slump and its impact on earnings. Qualcomm currently holds a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) due to these mixed signals.

item.title: [AAPL Bearish (-0.26)] Bias in the news feed? Apple, Google face scrutiny
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Bearish (-0.26)
Apple News and Google News are under scrutiny after a conservative media watchdog, the Media Research Center (MRC), reported that the news organizations they most frequently promote have not endorsed Republican presidential candidates in the last 10 elections. The MRC study found that the top outlets promoted by these tech giants exclusively endorsed Democratic candidates, leading to accusations of left-wing bias. Google disputes the findings, citing that publication prominence reflects high volume coverage on trending topics rather than bias, while Apple has not commented.

item.title: [AMZN Bullish (+0.23)] Sysco Taps Former Amazon Executive, Aramark CFO to Board as AI Push Accelerates
item.description:
Sentiment: AMZN Bullish (+0.23)
Sysco Corporation is expanding its board with two new directors, Jason Murray (former Amazon executive and Shipium CEO) and Tom Ondrof (former Aramark CFO), effective September 1st, to accelerate its AI-driven transformation. The company has also renamed its Technology Committee to the Artificial Intelligence Transformation & Technology Committee, reflecting its deepened commitment to AI. Sysco projects $100 million in AI-driven cost savings by fiscal 2027, contributing to revenue growth of 6-7% and adjusted EPS growth of 9-11%.

item.title: [AMZN Neutral (+0.14)] Food distributor Sysco adds two board members to advance AI transformation
item.description:

The food distributor expects these changes and AI-driven process improvements to generate $100 million in savings by fiscal 2027, contributing to significant revenue and adjusted EPS growth. The company also renamed its Technology Committee to the Artificial Intelligence Transformation & Technology Committee, reflecting its strategic focus on AI.

item.title: [AAPL Neutral (-0.15)] Xiao-I plans to exchange every seven American depositary shares for one on or about Sept. 8
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Neutral (-0.15)
Xiao-I (NASDAQ: AIXI) announced a planned change to its American Depositary Share (ADS) ratio, moving from one ADS representing 60 ordinary shares to one ADS representing 420 ordinary shares. This effectively acts as a one-for-seven reverse ADS split, expected around September 8, 2026. Existing ADSs held in DTC will be automatically exchanged, with fractional entitlements sold for cash.

item.title: [MSFT Bullish (+0.34)] The AI-Powered Go-to-Market Organization Isn’t Just a Vision Anymore
item.description:

Author Jan Gilg highlights five key areas where AI is already showing results in the customer journey: segmentation, engagement, deal execution, post-sale time-to-value, and retention/expansion. The piece emphasizes that successful organizations are deliberate about where AI adds real value for customers, focusing on clearing information, authority, and action gaps.

item.description:

item.description:

AbbVie eyes $325, propelled by the growth of Skyrizi and Rinvoq, along with an acquisition.

item.title: [AAPL Bullish (+0.41)] Micron Unveils Micron Research Labs, a U.S.-Based Long-Horizon Innovation Hub to Shape the Future of Memory and AI
item.description:
Sentiment: AAPL Bullish (+0.41)
Micron Technology has announced the establishment of Micron Research Labs, a new U.S.-based innovation hub dedicated to advancing memory and AI technologies. Backed by a $10 billion investment over the next decade, the lab will foster collaboration among academia, government, startups, and industry to drive breakthroughs beyond current technology roadmaps. This initiative aims to solidify America's leadership in the AI economy by focusing on critical memory technologies, advanced architectures, packaging, and future semiconductor manufacturing.

item.title: [MSFT Bullish (+0.21)] Oppenheimer reiterates Outperform on Salesforce stock ahead of earnings
item.description:

Guidance for 13% to 14% Q3 current remaining performance obligation growth could boost the stock's multiples, supporting a revenue reacceleration narrative in the second half of fiscal 2027.

item.title: [TSM Bearish (-0.20)] Does Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) Risk Losing AI Chip Orders To Capacity Limits?
item.description:
Sentiment: TSM Bearish (-0.20)
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) is facing capacity constraints due to surging AI chip demand, leading major clients like Qualcomm, Nvidia, Tesla, and Google to consider Samsung for advanced chip production. This diversification by tech giants aims to secure supply and reduce reliance on a single foundry, reflecting the significant impact of AI workloads on the supply chain. While Samsung's ability to increase foundry prices indicates strong overall AI demand, TSM's future performance will depend on how major customers split new advanced node and packaging orders between TSM and Samsung in upcoming product cycles.
